title: Separable Phrasal Verbs: Turn It Off
grammarTitle: Separable Phrasal Verbs — When You Can Split Them
grammarNote: Разделяемые фразовые глаголы (separable phrasal verbs) можно разделить, поместив объект МЕЖДУ глаголом и частицей. Но есть важное правило: если объект — это МЕСТОИМЕНИЕ (it, him, her, them и т.д.), его ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО нужно поставить между глаголом и частицей. Никогда нельзя говорить "turn off it" — только "turn it off".

grammarTable.subject: Separable (noun object)
grammarTable.verb: verb + particle + noun OR verb + noun + particle
grammarTable.example: "Turn OFF the light." OR "Turn the light OFF." — both correct with noun.

grammarTable.subject: Separable (pronoun!)
grammarTable.example: "Turn IT off." ✅ NEVER "Turn off it." ✗ — pronoun must go between!

grammarTable.subject: turn off
grammarTable.example: "Turn off your phone." / "Turn it off." / "Turn your phone off."

grammarTable.subject: switch on
grammarTable.example: "Switch on the laptop." / "Switch it on." / "Switch the laptop on."

grammarTable.subject: fill in
grammarTable.example: "Fill in the form." / "Fill it in." / "Fill the form in."

grammarTable.subject: pick up
grammarTable.example: "Pick up the book." / "Pick it up." / "Pick the book up."

grammarExtra.title: The key rule: pronouns MUST go inside

rows.example: "Turn off the light." ✅ / "Turn the light off." ✅ — BOTH correct!
"Turn it off." ✅ / ✗ "Turn off it." — NEVER correct!
"Give it up." / "Set it up." / "Sort it out." ✅ — always split with pronouns.

rows.form: Test: can I say "turn off it?"
rows.example: ❌ No → must be "turn IT off." The pronoun goes BETWEEN verb and particle.
"Turn on the heating." / "Turn it on." (activate/deactivate)
"Pick up the package." / "Pick it up." (collect/lift)
"Put down the bag." / "Put it down." (place somewhere lower)
"Fill in the form." / "Fill it in." (complete a document)
"Set up a meeting." / "Set it up." (arrange/organise)
"Sort out the problem." / "Sort it out." (resolve)
"Put off the meeting." / "Put it off." (postpone)
"Bring up the topic." / "Bring it up." (mention/raise)
"Find out the answer." / "Find it out." (discover)
"Write down the address." / "Write it down." (record on paper)
"Look up the word." / "Look it up." (search in a reference)
"Give up the idea." / "Give it up." (stop doing/abandon)

grammarExtra.title: Long noun objects — put them after the particle

rows.example: "Turn the light off." ✅ or "Turn off the light." ✅
"Turn off all the lights in the building." ✅ (NOT "turn all the lights in the building off" — too awkward!)
Short or pronoun → prefer split. Long phrase → after particle.

grammarExtra.title: ❌ Common mistakes with separable phrasal verbs

rows.example: ✅ "Turn IT off." — pronoun ALWAYS inside!
✅ "Set IT up." — pronoun must go between verb and particle!
✅ "I sorted IT out." — never particle + pronoun!
✅ "She picked ME up." — pronoun between!

grammarTip:
Разделяемые фразовые глаголы — главное правило:

С СУЩЕСТВИТЕЛЬНЫМ — оба варианта верны:
"Turn OFF the light." ✅
"Turn the light OFF." ✅

С МЕСТОИМЕНИЕМ — только ВНУТРИ:
"Turn IT off." ✅
✗ "Turn off IT." — НИКОГДА!

💡 Простой тест: замени существительное на местоимение.
Если местоимение оказалось перед частицей → ошибка!
"Turn it off" ✅ / "Turn off it" ✗

Частые разделяемые глаголы:
turn on/off, pick up, put down, set up, sort out,
fill in, find out, bring up, look up, give up

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct position for the pronoun.
exercises.text: The TV is too loud. Please ___ .
exercises.hint: Pronoun (it) must go BETWEEN verb and particle. "Please TURN IT OFF." ✅

exercises.text: She forgot to fill in the form. She forgot to fill ___ .
exercises.hint: Pronoun: "She forgot to fill IT IN." ✅ (pronoun inside) vs noun: "fill the form in" OR "fill in the form" — both OK.

exercises.instruction: Replace the noun with a pronoun and rewrite.
exercises.hint: Pronoun (it) goes inside: "Set IT UP." ✅ Never "Set up it."

exercises.instruction: Which sentence has the pronoun in the CORRECT position?
exercises.text: Choose the correct sentence with a pronoun.
exercises.hint: "She looked IT up." ✅ — pronoun must go between "looked" and "up". (Others: "looked up it" = ✗, "looked up/the word up" = ✅ with noun).

exercises.instruction: Complete with the phrasal verb + pronoun.
Choose the best position for a long noun phrase.
exercises.text: "Please turn ___ all the lights in every room of the building."
exercises.hint: Long noun phrase → put after the particle. "Please turn OFF all the lights in every room..." ✅ (Long phrases go after the particle to avoid awkwardness.)

exercises.text: "Can you sort out it?" is a correct sentence.
exercises.hint: ✅ "Can you sort IT OUT?" — pronoun goes INSIDE, between verb and particle. "Sort out it" = ✗ never!

exercises.text: "She picked up the keys." → She picked ___.
exercises.hint: "She picked THEM up." ✅ — pronoun (them) goes between "picked" and "up".

exercises.text: "The answer is wrong. Let me ___ (find the answer / look it up)."
exercises.correct: find it out / look it up
exercises.hint: "find out" or "look up" = to discover/research. With pronoun: "find IT out" / "look IT up." ✅

exercises.instruction: Which two sentences are BOTH correct?
exercises.text: "Give up the plan." — which two versions are correct?
opts: "Give up the plan" and "give the plan up"
exercises.correct: "Give up the plan" and "give the plan up"
exercises.hint: With noun: both "give UP the plan" and "give the plan UP" are correct! With pronoun: "give IT up" ✅ only.

exercises.text: "I'll set it up" is the only correct form with the pronoun "it".
exercises.hint: "Set it up" ✅ is the ONLY correct form with pronoun. "Set up it" ✗ is always wrong.

exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the pronoun in the correct position.
exercises.text: "We need to bring up the topic." → "We need to bring ___ ."
exercises.hint: Pronoun inside: "We need to bring IT UP." ✅

questions.text: "Turn off the light." — Can you also say "Turn the light off"?
opts: Yes — both are correct with a noun
No — only the first is correct
questions.correct: Yes — both are correct with a noun
questions.hint: With nouns: BOTH positions work. "Turn OFF the light." / "Turn the light OFF." ✅
Pronoun MUST go between verb and particle. "Turn IT off." ✅ NOT "Turn off it."

questions.text: "She looked up it." — What is wrong?
opts: The pronoun must go between — "looked it up"
questions.correct: The pronoun must go between — "looked it up"
questions.hint: ✅ "She looked IT up." — pronoun always inside with separable phrasal verbs!

questions.text: "I need to sort out the problem." → "I need to sort ___ ."
"Pick up the book." Which is correct with a pronoun?
questions.hint: "Pick IT up." ✅ — pronoun between verb and particle.
✅ "Set IT up." — NEVER "Set up it" with a pronoun!

questions.text: "Put off the meeting." With a pronoun becomes:
When must a pronoun go between the verb and the particle?
opts: Always — with both nouns and pronouns
Only with pronouns (it, him, her, them)
questions.correct: Only with pronouns (it, him, her, them)
questions.hint: With PRONOUNS: must go inside. "Turn it off." With NOUNS: both positions are fine.
"Give IT up." ✅ — pronoun goes between "give" and "up".

questions.text: "Find out the answer." Which is correct?
opts: "Find out the answer" and "find the answer out"
questions.correct: "Find out the answer" and "find the answer out"
questions.hint: With noun: both positions work. "Find OUT the answer" ✅ / "Find the answer OUT" ✅.

questions.text: "Can you bring up the issue?" → "Can you bring ___ ?"
questions.hint: Pronoun inside: "Can you bring IT UP?" ✅

questions.text: Where does a long noun phrase go with a separable phrasal verb?
opts: At the start of the sentence
questions.hint: Long phrases go AFTER the particle. "Turn off all the lights in the building." ✅ (not split)

questions.text: "She turned the television off." — Is this correct?
opts: Yes — with a noun, the split is acceptable
No — should be "turned off the television"
questions.correct: Yes — with a noun, the split is acceptable
questions.hint: "She turned THE TELEVISION OFF." ✅ — with a noun, either position is fine.

questions.text: "I need to look up this word." → "I need to look ___ ."
questions.hint: Pronoun (it) inside: "I need to look IT UP." ✅

questions.text: Which sentence uses a separable phrasal verb CORRECTLY with a pronoun?
questions.hint: "She sorted IT out." ✅ — pronoun between "sorted" and "out". ("sorted out the problem" also ✅ with noun)
